lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Add a concise target-oriented summary.
items.because: A recruiter currently has to infer whether you are pursuing quantitative research, quantitative development, statistical modeling, or academia.

items.says: Reorder sections so Northpeak Capital and the volatility project are more prominent than Sunrise Bakery and teaching.
items.because: A recruiter scanning for quant experience may otherwise assume that store management is your current professional direction.

items.says: Reduce the visual emphasis on the B.S. relative to the Ph.D.
items.because: Your graduate training is the more important signal for the target role.

items.says: Remove or consolidate duplicated trading-signal claims.
items.because: The Northpeak section and Kaggle section appear to describe essentially the same order-book imbalance signal and performance result.

items.says: Correct the skills section and make it more specific.
items.because: There is a spelling error, one unexplained technology, and insufficient detail about the tools used for research and production-quality workflows.

items.says: Verify that the code link goes to a real, polished portfolio.
items.because: An empty or generic repository can hurt more than having no link.

items.says: Add a location or work-authorization signal if relevant to your target market.
items.because: This is especially useful for finance employers that recruit by office or require specific authorization.

items.says: Consider adding a LinkedIn profile only if it is complete and consistent with the resume.
items.because: An incomplete profile creates an avoidable credibility issue.

items.says: Do not add a generic objective statement.
items.because: What is missing is a concise professional positioning summary, not an objective.

items.says: Add your research area or dissertation topic.
items.because: Quantitative research readers need to know whether your work involves time series, statistical learning, econometrics, optimization, high-dimensional inference, or another relevant area.

items.says: Clarify whether the Ph.D. is in progress, completed, or expected to be completed before the target role begins.
items.because: The expected date is useful, but the resume should make your availability and candidacy status unambiguous.

items.says: Add a small number of highly relevant courses only if they strengthen the target.
items.because: Relevant examples would include time-series analysis, stochastic processes, optimization, numerical methods, or financial econometrics.

items.says: Include your advisor, dissertation title, or research group only if those details are meaningful for the role.
items.because: They can help for research-heavy quant positions, but they are less valuable for purely engineering-oriented roles.

items.says: Consider removing the undergraduate degree if space is needed.
items.because: Because you are near completion of a Ph.D., the B.S. is no longer essential unless the institution or degree provides a particularly useful signal.

items.says: Move this role below Northpeak Capital and the university research experience, or place it in a separate 'Additional Experience' section.
items.because: A recruiter scanning for quant experience may otherwise assume that store management is your current professional direction.

items.says: Make the scale and ownership clearer.
items.because: The bullet currently combines shift management, team supervision, and labor-budget control without showing the degree of responsibility or result.

items.says: Add a measurable budget or operational outcome if one exists.
items.because: 'Within budget' is a baseline expectation rather than a strong accomplishment unless you can show the size of the budget, savings, or improvement.

items.says: Clarify whether you supervised employees directly or coordinated their work.
items.because: This distinction matters for leadership credibility.

items.says: Explain the mechanism at a high level.
items.because: The current wording says you ran counts and placed orders, but not what analytical or operational change caused the reduction.

items.says: Avoid overstating the quantitative sophistication.
items.because: Present it as a measurable operations improvement, not as a forecasting model unless you actually built one.

items.says: Specify the metric represented by 'risk-adjusted returns.'
items.because: A technical reader will want to know whether this means Sharpe ratio, information ratio, return per unit of volatility, or another measure.

items.says: Clarify the comparison period, universe, transaction-cost assumptions, and baseline.
items.because: Without these, the 35% figure is difficult to evaluate and may appear inflated.

items.says: Reconcile this claim with the later Sharpe-ratio claim.
items.because: The resume currently reports both a 35% improvement and an increase from 1.1 to 1.5. Those may be consistent, but the relationship is not obvious.

items.says: Identify your individual contribution to the smoother.
items.because: Make sure the bullet accurately distinguishes your work from the desk’s existing signal.

items.says: State what was being validated.
items.because: The reader should know whether this was the smoother, the signal, the full strategy, or a research pipeline.

items.says: Clarify the embargo design if it was a meaningful part of the methodology.
items.because: A quant interviewer may ask what interval was embargoed and why.

items.says: Avoid presenting the validation method as proof of live performance.
items.because: It supports the credibility of the backtest but does not establish that the strategy will work live.

items.says: Specify the implementation and engineering scope.
items.because: A quant developer or research engineering reviewer will want to know whether you handled point-in-time correctness, feature versioning, storage, latency, testing, or deployment.

items.says: Explain what 'reused in two later signal projects' means.
items.because: Clarify whether the team reused the infrastructure, the features, or both.

items.says: Clarify your role in the live allocation decision.
items.because: Portfolio managers approving a small allocation is strong evidence, but it should not imply that you managed capital or made the final investment decision.

items.says: Add the scale or risk limits of the allocation if permitted.
items.because: A small live allocation is otherwise difficult to interpret.

items.says: Identify the failure cases you presented.
items.because: Demonstrating that you examined failure modes is valuable, but the current wording leaves that evidence underdeveloped.

items.says: Remove this bullet or substantially correct its methodological framing.
items.because: Selecting the best configuration from 400 trials and then calling its in-sample or selected Sharpe the 'expected live Sharpe' is a classic multiple-testing and selection-bias problem.

items.says: Do not claim an expected live Sharpe unless it was estimated using an independent holdout, nested validation, or another defensible procedure.
items.because: A technical reviewer may reject the entire research section if this remains unchanged.

items.says: Determine whether this is the same signal described in the Kaggle project.
items.because: If it is the same work, remove the duplicate from one section and keep the more credible, better-contextualized version.

items.says: Clarify what 'the desk book' means.
items.because: It is not immediately clear whether this was an existing portfolio, a simulated book, or a research portfolio.

items.says: Clarify the source of the 18-month out-of-sample period.
items.because: State whether it was truly untouched during model selection and whether the period includes transaction costs, slippage, capacity constraints, and changing market regimes.

items.says: Avoid presenting a Sharpe increase alone as evidence of production readiness.
items.because: Add the relevant constraints or supporting diagnostics if available.

items.says: Correct or clarify the random-number-generation description.
items.because: Saying that every worker used 'the same random seed' can imply that workers generated identical or correlated random streams, which would undermine the simulation.

items.says: State whether you used independent reproducible streams or separate worker seeds.
items.because: Reproducibility is positive; duplicated random streams are not.

items.says: Add the implementation environment if relevant.
items.because: For quant research roles, parallel computing, vectorization, cluster execution, or job scheduling can be useful signals.

items.says: Make authorship and publication status precise.
items.because: 'My proof' and 'is now Section 3' may overstate your role or imply acceptance when the paper is only under review.

items.says: Identify whether you are first author, coauthor, or contributor.
items.because: This matters to technical reviewers.

items.says: Use the exact status of the manuscript consistently.
items.because: Under review, submitted, revise-and-resubmit, accepted, and published have materially different credibility.

items.says: Move this below the research and software bullets.
items.because: It is a positive teaching and communication signal but is not among your strongest quant credentials.

items.says: Keep the teaching rating only if the source and scale are legitimate.
items.because: A 4.8/5 rating is useful, but it should not receive more emphasis than research results.

items.says: Clarify whether you designed the course material or only delivered assigned recitations.
items.because: This determines the level of ownership.

items.says: Move this bullet ahead of teaching.
items.because: It demonstrates software development, public delivery, and adoption.

items.says: Clarify how downloads are measured.
items.because: Downloads from CRAN, GitHub, or another source carry different meanings.

items.says: Add evidence of quality if available.
items.because: Tests, documentation, continuous integration, external contributors, or use in research would strengthen the claim.

items.says: Keep the package name or link if it is publicly available and polished.
items.because: This is one of the best opportunities to substantiate your technical claims.

items.says: Clarify the data period and forecast horizon.
items.because: These materially affect the interpretation of the result.

items.says: Specify whether the evaluation was fully out of sample and how hyperparameters were selected.
items.because: The current wording is promising but not enough to establish that the comparison is fair.

items.says: Explain why a temporal convolutional model was appropriate.
items.because: This can be addressed in the project link or interview, but the resume should show the methodological reasoning if space allows.

items.says: Clarify the unit of the 5% result.
items.because: The reader should know whether the test was performed separately for each index, across forecast horizons, or in another structure.

items.says: State whether the crisis-period result was pre-specified or selected after examining the data.
items.because: This affects the credibility of the robustness claim.

items.says: Avoid allowing the statistical test detail to overwhelm the practical result.
items.because: The bullet should support the forecasting claim rather than read like a methods appendix.

items.says: Clarify the paper’s status.
items.because: 'Working paper' is appropriate, but do not let it be mistaken for a publication.

items.says: Add the paper or presentation link if available.
items.because: A technical reviewer will want to inspect the methodology.

items.says: State whether you were the sole author or part of a team.
items.because: This is important for evaluating ownership.

items.says: Add the competition result or remove the bullet.
items.because: As written, it describes activities without showing performance, ranking, or a concrete technical outcome.

items.says: Specify the dataset or prediction task only if it helps explain the relevance.
items.because: Generic competition language does not differentiate you.

items.says: Clarify whether the improvement was measured by reducing overestimation, improving leaderboard performance, or both.
items.because: 'Closed a 0.02 gap' is not automatically a positive result unless the reader understands what the gap represents.

items.says: Avoid presenting this as independent evidence if it is connected to the Northpeak work.
items.because: The resume should distinguish academic, competition, and professional work clearly.

items.says: Investigate and resolve the apparent duplication with Northpeak’s final bullet.
items.because: This is the most serious issue in the Projects section.

items.says: If it is a separate experiment, explain the difference in dataset, signal, period, and portfolio construction.
items.because: Otherwise, remove it from the Kaggle section.

items.says: Do not claim ownership of a 'futures book' if this was only a simulated competition portfolio.
items.because: Use terminology that accurately reflects the environment.

items.says: Avoid repeating the same 18-month period and same signal concept in two locations.
items.because: Repetition makes the resume look padded and may prompt questions about whether the results are being double-counted.

items.says: Add the specific tools used in the experience bullets.
items.because: The resume currently mentions Python, R, PyTorch, and Kafka but does not show enough evidence of how each was used.

items.says: Only retain Kafka if you used it meaningfully.
items.because: It currently appears without any supporting experience, which can look like keyword stuffing.

items.says: Consider including relevant data and research tooling if accurate.
items.because: Examples of categories to evaluate include SQL, version control, testing, numerical libraries, distributed computing, databases, and cloud or cluster tooling.

items.says: Separate research languages from production or infrastructure tools.
items.because: This helps readers understand your technical profile.

items.says: Correct 'econometircs' to 'econometrics.'
items.because: A spelling error in a core target-domain skill is especially damaging.

items.says: Use consistent and conventional method names.
items.because: 'Time-series econometrics' should be presented consistently with the terminology used in your projects and publications.

items.says: Add methods demonstrated by the resume.
items.because: Your experience supports areas such as point-in-time validation, walk-forward testing, multiple-testing correction, volatility forecasting, microstructure features, high-dimensional statistics, Monte Carlo simulation, and statistical inference.

items.says: Do not list methods you cannot discuss deeply.
items.because: Quant interviews often probe every method named in the skills section.

items.says: Consider including portfolio and market methods only if they are genuinely part of your expertise.
items.because: For example, transaction-cost modeling, capacity estimation, signal evaluation, and risk adjustment should appear only if you can explain the implementation and assumptions.
